speeches.speaker: Peter Dutton
speeches.brief: Moved the Private Health Insurance Amendment Bill, which pauses indexation of income thresholds for the private health insurance rebate and Medicare levy surcharge for three years, saying only about four per cent of the 6.2 million private health insurance policies held in December 2013 would be affected, while overall health spending rises from $68 billion to $79 billion by 2017-18.

speeches.speaker: Angus Taylor
speeches.brief: Argued in support of the Private Health Insurance Amendment Bill, saying it would pause private health insurance rebate and Medicare levy surcharge indexation for three years, affecting only about four per cent of the 6.2 million policies held in December 2013, with savings funding a $20 billion Medical Research Future Fund expected to eventually deliver an extra $1 billion a year to research.

speeches.speaker: Nick Champion
speeches.brief: Argued in support of the Private Health Insurance Amendment Bill, saying its $599 million in savings follows the previous government's $3 billion savings from means-testing the private health insurance rebate, which funded cancer centres at the Lyell McEwin, Gawler and Clare hospitals in his electorate.

speeches.speaker: Andrew Laming
speeches.brief: Argued in support of the Private Health Insurance Amendment Bill, saying freezing indexation of Medicare levy surcharge tiers would direct extra contributions from higher income earners into the Medical Research Future Fund, and said up to two million of the 13 million Australians with private cover had downgraded their policies after Labor's earlier means-testing changes.

speeches.speaker: Warren Snowdon
speeches.brief: Argued against the Private Health Insurance Amendment Bill, saying its $599.3 million in savings from pausing indexation would shift health costs onto consumers and fund the Medical Research Future Fund rather than health care, and cited Australian Diagnostic Imaging Association figures showing patients could face up to $2207 for a liver metastasis diagnosis under the government's changes.

speeches.speaker: Andrew Southcott
speeches.brief: Argued in support of the Private Health Insurance Amendment Bill, saying its $599 million savings measure would affect only four per cent of the 6.2 million private health insurance policies and fund a $20 billion Medical Research Future Fund expected to double annual medical research spending with an extra $1 billion a year.

speeches.speaker: Shayne Neumann
speeches.brief: Argued against the Private Health Insurance Amendment Bill, saying its $599.3 million in savings should fund Medicare rather than the medical research fund, and cited Queensland Treasurer Tim Nicholls' warning that the government's $50 billion in hospital funding cuts would mean fewer doctors and nurses and longer waiting times.

speeches.speaker: Andrew Robb
speeches.brief: Summed up the bill, saying it pauses private health insurance rebate income thresholds at 2014-15 rates for three years, will not affect individuals earning $90,000 or less or families earning $180,000 or less, and warned that without budget repair the government's interest bill could grow to $3 billion a month, or $36 billion a year.
